main_text.l: Dicere, Prisce, iuvat: dicentem sedulus audi:
Hoc quoque ne pereas naufragus ipse mari.
Aeolus hic Vera est magnorum, crede, figura,
Est quibus in toto Vanitas orbe nihil.
AEolia aula quid est, nisi quas nos cernimus
aulas?
Nempe aliud rediens rursus in orbe Chaos.
Hinc Euri, Corique ruunt, hinc nubilus Auster,
Hinc Aquilo rigido iussus ab axe volat.
Hinc mundi pelagus vertuntque ruuntque procellae,
Rarus ut his curat nauita tutus aquis.
Ia sunt Aeolides, loca foeta furentibus
Austris.
Aspice disruptas undique, Prisce, rates:
Et si forte sapis, curvum in contraria flecte:
Stultus, ab hac vitam qui sibi morte petit.
IN TVRNONVM, indoctum qui-
dem, sed doctorum non paucorum
Mecœnatem.
Indoctus doctos pascis, Turnone, beatus,
Sit tam animo saperes, quam tibi mensa sapit.
Iunge tamen, Musa, Vestras alere improbus artes
Quum detrectet honos, sic modo pascat ut.
M

page.notes: Verse lines in the first block are printed in italic with long s and ligatures; some words are doubtful (e.g. "Vera", "Vanitas", "Vestras", "ut" at line end, "Sit tam animo saperes" as printed). Lines 12–13 and the final two lines of the second poem are hard to read and may be imperfect. The "M" at the foot is a gathering signature, not text; it is transcribed as printed in the main text and may be better placed as a signature.
